Cortical auditory evoked potentials are late responses from the auditory cortex.
In young children, the most prominent wave is a broad P1.
In newborns, P1 latency is long, about 300 milliseconds.
It shortens with age, reaching about 60 milliseconds by around age 20.
So P1 latency serves as a measure of central auditory maturation.
